text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

## Abstract  
We evaluated whether the GEO accession “GSE309890” is synonymous with “GDS309890.”  Using the GEO‐specific `geo_series` tool (NCBI E-utilities esummary wrapper), we queried each accession independently.  The Series accession GSE309890 resolved to a valid GEO Series (entry type = GSE) with UID 200309890, describing an RNA-seq study of sertraline-induced antibiotic-resistance evolution in *Escherichia coli*.  In contrast, the putative DataSet accession “GDS309890” returned an empty record: all descriptive fields were blank and no entry_type was assigned.  These results show that (i) GSE309890 exists as a Series and (ii) no curated DataSet (GDS) bearing the numeric identifier 309890 is present in GEO.  Because GDS identifiers are assigned only after manual curation of selected Series, most Series—including GSE309890—never receive a GDS counterpart.  Therefore, GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same; only the Series record is available.  This clarification prevents mis-referencing and guides users to the correct accession for data retrieval.

## I. Introduction  
Background.  NCBI’s Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) stores functional-genomics data.  Primary submitter-supplied studies are registered as Series accessions (prefix “GSE”).  A small, manually curated subset of biologically coherent Series are reissued as DataSets (prefix “GDS”) after internal GEO curation.  
Literature Review.  No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap.  Users often assume every GSE automatically has a corresponding GDS accession; it is unclear whether this holds for GSE309890.  
Objective & Hypothesis.  Objective: determine whether GSE309890 has a corresponding GDS record (GDS309890) and if the two accessions reference the same study.  Hypothesis: GSE309890 exists as a Series, but a GDS309890 record may not exist because most Series are not curated into DataSets.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design.  Presence or absence of records was assessed by direct lookup of each accession with GEO’s esummary API via the `geo_series` tool, which resolves accessions and returns structured metadata.  
Materials.  
1. GEO database (queried through NCBI E-utilities).  
2. MCP `geo_series` tool for accession resolution.  
Procedures.  
• Call 1: `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=FALSE)`  
• Call 2: `geo_series(accession="GDS309890", list_files=FALSE)`  
Statistical Analysis.  Binary outcome (record found vs. not found) determined by non-empty `entry_type` and presence of metadata fields.  Denominator = 2 accession queries; numerator = 1 valid record.

## III. Results  
Data Presentation.  

Table 1. Resolution status of queried accessions.  

| Accession | UID        | entry_type | title present? |
|-----------|------------|-----------|----------------|
| GSE309890 | 200309890 | GSE (Series) | Yes |
| GDS309890 | 309890    | (none)    | No |

Findings.  One of two queried accessions (50 %) resolved to a valid record.  GSE309890 is a GEO Series with full metadata, whereas GDS309890 returned no curated DataSet record.

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation.  The existence of GSE309890 and the absence of GDS309890 indicate that the study has not been curated into a GEO DataSet.  Consequently, GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not equivalent.  
Context.  GEO curates only a fraction of Series into DataSets; the majority remain as Series only.  Users seeking processed data must therefore reference the GSE accession and download supplementary files from the Series FTP directory.  
Limitations.  The analysis relies solely on current GEO/NCBI E-utilities records; future curation could create a GDS accession.  No direct PubMed link was present, so publication status remains undetermined.  
Conclusion & Future Directions.  Researchers should cite and download data using GSE309890.  Periodic re-checks could detect if a GDS record is added later.

## References  
[1] NCBI GEO esummary for GSE309890. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0  
[2] NCBI GEO esummary for GDS309890. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=309890&version=2.0  

## Acknowledgments  
Data were obtained from the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) via the NCBI E-utilities API.
